data.title: NextDC's Prudence Is Positive Amid Uncertainty — Market Talk
data.description: NextDC's prudent spending is greeted with approval at Jefferies as the future of its troubled Melbourne data center remains unclear. Analyst Roger Samuel sees the data-center operator's capital preservation as a positive, and notes that the company could sell some of its A$750 million land bank if needed. However, there is still no settled solution to its power-line problems at the M3 center. Samuel tells clients in a note that there is also uncertainty over Goodman and Digital Realty's intentions for their 9.9% stake in NextDC. Jefferies raises its target price on the stock 31% to 8.90 Australian dollars and maintains a hold rating. Shares are up 0.7% at A$9.075. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)

data.title: South Korea's education minister quits over exam cheating chaos
data.description:
South Korean Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned on Sunday, taking responsibility for confusion caused by last-minute measures to prevent AI-assisted cheating in the country's high-stakes college entrance examination held last week.

  • President Lee Jae Myung accepted the resignation within an hour and ordered a comprehensive review of national exam management and related laws.

  • The government rushed out tighter restrictions after the top scorer in a national tax-accountant examination admitted using a miniature camera, a smartphone and artificial intelligence to cheat.

  • During the eight-hour exam, authorities restricted Wi-Fi, checked glasses and clothing buttons for hidden devices, and issued nationwide alerts to detect concealed phones.

  • More than 550,000 students registered for the test, which plays a major role in admission to the country's top universities.

  • Choi acknowledged that inadequate preparation and repeated rule changes had inconvenienced students and officials.

  • He also faced criticism after saying that, because of his age, he did not think he could detect AI-assisted cheating.

  • The heightened precautions last week uncovered dozens of prohibited mobile phones, although it was unclear whether all were intended for cheating.

data.title: US futures bounce while Asia markets brace for AI wipeout
data.description:
US stock futures attempted a recovery on Monday, while Asian markets slid and authorities around the region readied support measures after a withering wipeout last week for tech and chip stocks at the centre of the AI boom.

Investors are questioning whether the vast sums of mostly borrowed money spent building data centres to power AI models will generate returns fast enough to repay lenders and big enough to justify some of the high stock prices.

Last week's 10% drop in the Nasdaq was its largest weekly drop since pandemic panic gripped markets in March 2020.

Nasdaq 100 futures bounced nearly 3% in early trade on Monday, and S&P 500 futures rose by 2%.

South Korea's chip-heavy KOSPI dropped more than 3% in the first few minutes of morning trade.

Japan markets are closed for a holiday on Monday but futures indicate selling pressure, while Hang Seng futures (HSIc1) also point to a fall. Australian stocks were slightly lower.

The "AI trade" has for several years lifted a wide range of stocks, from switch and cable makers to electricity generators and the manufacturers of anything in the computing supply chain, but they have been under pressure in recent months from rising interest rates.

AI-related shares took a particularly sharp downturn last week as the exit of Jensen Huang, the Nvidia CEO nicknamed the "godfather of AI", and the faltering debut of AI company Anthropic , which closed 8.5% lower on its first full day of trading, pointed to a souring mood.

Taiwanese shares TWSE:TAIEX were down 17% for the week, their biggest weekly fall since 1990, and Friday's 10% drop for the Philadelphia semiconductor index points to more pain for Asia's chip-heavy markets, especially in Taiwan and South Korea.

Taiwan's financial regulator on Saturday ordered a further tightening of short-selling rules for stocks, while in China stock exchanges announced a batch of support measures such as easing requirements for margin financing.

South Korea will be ready to deploy market stabilisation funds immediately should the market continue to fall, the finance ministry said on Sunday, after the benchmark index last week slumped to 10-month lows.

data.title: Asian Currencies Mixed as Traders Digest Divergent Signals — Market Talk
data.description: Asian currencies are mixed against the dollar as traders digest divergent signals. On the one hand, higher U.S. stock futures in early Asian session could buoy appetite for risky assets. On the other hand, "hawkish Fed commentary and FOMC minutes have supported the U.S. dollar," StoneX's Matt Simpson says in commentary. data.title: Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: Flash PMI Data to Provide Gauge on Economic Growth
data.description:
By Dow Jones Newswires staff

Below are the most important global events likely to affect FX and bond markets in the week starting Nov. 23.

November's flash purchasing managers' surveys for the U.S., eurozone and U.K. will be among the key events. The surveys are an important measure of economic activity and could signal whether there is scope for the Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of England to raise interest rates further.

In the U.S, markets will also be closely monitoring Personal Consumption Expenditures price data, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation measure.

In the Asia-Pacific region, South Korea's interest-rate decision will lead the week, with most analysts expecting a quarter-point increase as strong chip exports fuel growth and inflation remains above target. Inflation data from Australia and Tokyo, along with remarks from a Bank of Japan policy board member, could shape expectations for rate increases in both countries.

China will report October industrial profits as investors watch for Beijing's response to tighter U.S. chip export restrictions.

U.S.

U.S. economic activity and inflation will help investors gauge the path of interest rates in a week shortened by a major holiday.

November's flash manufacturing and services PMI numbers are on tap Monday, as well as a speech by New York Federal Reserve President John Williams at the University of Mount Saint Vincent.

September housing indicators are likely to draw attention Tuesday, as elevated mortgage rates weigh on the sector.

The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index is also scheduled for Tuesday, as consumption continues to be a source of strength for the U.S. economy.

A second estimate of third-quarter gross domestic product growth is due Wednesday. The same day will bring the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the Personal Consumption Expenditures, as consumer prices keep rising faster than the 2% annual pace targeted by the central bank.

"The main message from the report is likely to be that pressure on goods prices is growing," economists at the Investment Institute by UniCredit said in a note. "Overall, October PCE data are likely to keep the Fed firmly on a hiking trajectory."

Durable goods orders, initial jobless claims and new home sales data are also due Wednesday along with the Summary of Commentary on Current Economic Conditions by Federal Reserve District, known as the Beige Book.

Markets will be closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving Holiday and will close early on Friday.

U.K.

The U.K. will have a relatively light data release calendar. The November flash estimate purchasing managers' index survey on Monday is the main event.

The U.K. composite PMI, a measure of manufacturing and services activity, rose to 52.9 in October, up from 52.0 in September and the highest reading since February.

"For the November report we imagine that the PMIs ticked higher again," Investec economists said in a note.

Activity might have received a boost from the absence of significant tax increases in the U.K. budget in October as some had feared, they said. U.S. President Trump refraining from renewed large-scale attacks on Iran following the midterm elections might have also helped, not least by helping to lower crude prices, they said. Investec forecasts the composite PMI will rise to 53.1 in November.

Elsewhere, the CBI distributive trades survey is due on Wednesday.

The U.K., meanwhile, plans to sell September 2049 index-linked gilt through syndicated sale, subject to demand and market conditions.

Eurozone

German, French and wider eurozone flash purchasing managers' surveys for November are due on Monday. The eurozone composite purchasing managers index, a measure of manufacturing and services activity, fell to a four-month low of 51.7 in October from 53.1 in September but remained above the 50 level that separates an expansion from a contraction.

"We expect to see some mild weakness in the euro-area PMIs, reflecting the challenging environment for energy markets and tighter financial conditions in Europe," RBC Capital Markets strategists said in a note.

On Tuesday, the German ifo business confidence survey for November will be released. That will be followed by the final third-quarter German gross domestic product report on Wednesday and GfK German consumer confidence survey for December on Thursday.

French and Spanish inflation data for November will be published Friday along with November German labor market data and the European Commission's business confidence survey.

Japan

Bank of Japan policy board member Naoki Tamura will meet with local leaders in the Yamanashi prefecture on Thursday. Investors will watch his remarks for clues on when the central bank might raise rates again.

Tokyo's November consumer-price data are due Friday. The figures are an early indicator of nationwide inflation, and a pickup could strengthen expectations for a rate increase.

BOJ Gov. Kazuo Ueda recently stressed the importance of keeping underlying inflation around the central bank's 2% target. He said inflation excluding fresh food is likely to rise well above 2% as companies pass on higher labor costs, oil prices remain high and the yen stays weak.

The Ministry of Finance will auction about 300 billion yen of 40-year government bonds on Wednesday, reopening an issue first sold in May. The sale could draw demand from insurers and pension funds seeking long-dated debt.

The BOJ is scheduled to buy government bonds in three maturity ranges on Thursday, including those with more than three and up to five years remaining and those with more than 10 and up to 25 years remaining.

Japanese markets will be closed Monday for a national holiday.

China

A thin data slate awaits in China. The sole release of note drops Friday, which will show how China's industrial firms fared in October.

Economists will look at the figures to see if industrial profit growth held up last month after surging in September. Spending tied to artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure has been a key driver of profits over the year, though that hasn't benefited all sectors evenly.

Focus will also be on any potential announcements from Beijing after Xi Jinping's meetings with Trump didn't yield much in the way of progress on key trade and geopolitical issues. Markets will be watching ministry statements closely after Chinese officials warned of potential countermeasures to U.S. moves to tighten chip-export restrictions.

Australia / New Zealand

Australia's October inflation report on Wednesday will help shape expectations for the Reserve Bank of Australia's December rate decision. In September, annual headline inflation rose to 4.3% and trimmed-mean inflation climbed to 3.6%.

Third-quarter capital spending data due Thursday will show how much businesses invested and whether they revised their spending plans. The RBA will publish its bulletin the same day.

In New Zealand, third-quarter retail sales data due Monday will show how household spending is holding up ahead of the central bank's Dec. 9 rate decision.

South Korea

Bank of Korea is expected to raise its benchmark rate by a quarter-percentage-point to 3.25% on Thursday after leaving it unchanged in October.

Some analysts also expect the bank to raise its growth and inflation forecasts for 2026 and 2027 as demand for chips used in artificial intelligence boosts exports and price pressures persist.

The central bank signaled it would raise its growth forecasts after third-quarter gross domestic product grew faster than expected. It expects inflation to stay above its 2% target through 2027.

The International Monetary Fund, the Korea Development Institute and Citi Research raised their growth forecasts for South Korea earlier this month, citing strength in the semiconductor industry.

Singapore

Singapore's consumer-price index likely rose 1.9% in October from a year earlier, down from 2.2% in September, according to the median estimate of six economists polled by The Wall Street Journal. Core inflation, which excludes private road transport and accommodation costs, likely slowed to 1.6% from 2.0%, the poll showed. The data are due Monday.

Lower fourth-quarter electricity tariffs and a high year-earlier comparison likely helped ease inflation, said UOB economist Jester Koh.

Final third-quarter gross domestic product figures are due Tuesday. An advance estimate showed the economy grew 5.4% from a year earlier. DBS economists expect that figure to be revised up to 5.6%, mainly because manufacturing grew faster than initially reported.

DBS expects the government to forecast growth of 2.5% to 4.5% for 2027.

Any references to days are in local times.

Write to Renae Dyer at renae.dyer@wsj.com and Jihye Lee at jihye.lee@wsj.com

data.title: MetaOptics Ltd Secures up to S$32 Million Share Subscription Facility from GEM Opportunities Fund ISA Ltd.
data.description:
Three-year committed facility provides MetaOptics with flexible growth capital, drawn down at the Company's sole discretion

SINGAPORE, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- MetaOptics Ltd (Catalist: 9MT) (OTCQX: MOTLY) ("MetaOptics" or the "Company", and together with its subsidiaries, the "Group"), a Singapore-headquartered semiconductor optics company pioneering glass-based metalens solutions enhanced by AI-driven image processing, announced that it had on 20 November 2026, entered into a share subscription facility agreement with GEM Opportunities Fund ISA Ltd. ("GEM"), the Bermuda-based investment vehicle managed by Global Emerging Markets (GEM), New York, for an aggregate commitment of up to S$32 million (the "Share Subscription Facility"). The Share Subscription Facility is subject to, inter alia, the approval of the Company's shareholders ("Shareholders") at an extraordinary general meeting ("EGM") to be convened. A circular containing further details of the Share Subscription Facility, together with the notice of EGM, will be despatched to Shareholders in due course.

The Company intends to apply the net proceeds from drawdowns under the Share Subscription Facility, entirely for the Group's working capital purposes, including general corporate expenses, funding the day-to-day operations of the Group and supporting the growth of its existing business. As part of the Group's plans to grow its existing business, the Group intends to establish a new 12-inch glass semiconductor fabrication line in the United States to produce metalenses for co-packaged optics ("CPO") and colour imaging applications. The Share Subscription Facility provides MetaOptics with flexible access to growth capital while allowing the Company to control the timing of any drawdowns, in line with its capital needs and prevailing market conditions.

Mr Thng Chong Kim, Executive Chairman of MetaOptics, said: "This Share Subscription Facility gives us a reliable, flexible source of capital for our day-to-day operations and to support the growth of our existing business by establishing a new 12-inch glass semiconductor fabrication line in the United States, on terms that put MetaOptics in control of the timing and size of each drawdown. We are pleased to have the backing of GEM, an experienced global investor, as we execute on our plans and build long-term value for our Shareholders."

This press release should be read in conjunction with the announcement released by the Company on SGXNet on 23 November 2026 in relation to the Share Subscription Facility.

About MetaOptics LtdMetaOptics Ltd (Catalist: 9MT) is a leading-edge semiconductor optics company pioneering glass-based metalens solutions enhanced by AI-driven image processing. Using advanced optical design and a scalable 12-inch DUV lithography process, it powers next-generation applications in CPO, mobile, AR/VR, automotive and other emerging markets. Headquartered in Singapore, MetaOptics aims to deliver high-performance optics with the reliability and scalability demanded by today's most innovative technology brands. Find out more at www.metaoptics.sg.

About GEMGEM (Global Emerging Markets) is a US$3.4 billion alternative investment group with operations in Paris, New York, Los Angeles and the Bahamas. GEM manages a diverse set of investment vehicles focused on emerging and developed markets and has completed over 600 transactions in 75 countries. Each investment vehicle has a different degree of operational control, risk-adjusted return and liquidity profile. Its family of funds and investment vehicles provides GEM and its partners with exposure to Small-Mid Cap Management Buyouts, Private Investments in Public Equities and select venture investments.  For more information, please visit www.gemny.com.

Forward-Looking StatementsThis press release contains forward-looking statements, including statements regarding the share subscription facility, the Company's intended use of proceeds and its business plans. These statements are based on the Company's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. The Facility is subject to shareholder approval at the EGM, and drawdowns under the Facility are subject to the satisfaction of certain conditions and to the execution of definitive documentation. There can be no assurance as to the amount or timing of any funds the Company may ultimately raise. The Company undertakes no obligation to update any forward-looking statements except as required by law.

The U.K. composite PMI, a measure of manufacturing and services activity, rose to 52.9 in October, up from 52.0 in September and the highest reading since February.

"For the November report we imagine that the PMIs ticked higher again," Investec economists said in a note.

Activity might have received a boost from the absence of significant tax increases in the U.K. budget in October as some had feared, they said. U.S. President Trump refraining from renewed large-scale attacks on Iran following the midterm elections might have also helped, not least by helping to lower crude prices, they said. Investec forecasts the composite PMI will rise to 53.1 in November.

Elsewhere, the CBI distributive trades survey is due on Wednesday.

The U.K., meanwhile, plans to sell September 2049 index-linked gilt through syndicated sale, subject to demand and market conditions.

Eurozone

German, French and wider eurozone flash purchasing managers' surveys for November are due on Monday. The eurozone composite purchasing managers index, a measure of manufacturing and services activity, fell to a four-month low of 51.7 in October from 53.1 in September but remained above the 50 level that separates an expansion from a contraction.

"We expect to see some mild weakness in the euro-area PMIs, reflecting the challenging environment for energy markets and tighter financial conditions in Europe," RBC Capital Markets strategists said in a note.

On Tuesday, the German ifo business confidence survey for November will be released. That will be followed by the final third-quarter German gross domestic product report on Wednesday and GfK German consumer confidence survey for December on Thursday.

French and Spanish inflation data for November will be published Friday along with November German labor market data and the European Commission's business confidence survey.

Japan

Bank of Japan policy board member Naoki Tamura will meet with local leaders in the Yamanashi prefecture on Thursday. Investors will watch his remarks for clues on when the central bank might raise rates again.

Tokyo's November consumer-price data are due Friday. The figures are an early indicator of nationwide inflation, and a pickup could strengthen expectations for a rate increase.

BOJ Gov. Kazuo Ueda recently stressed the importance of keeping underlying inflation around the central bank's 2% target. He said inflation excluding fresh food is likely to rise well above 2% as companies pass on higher labor costs, oil prices remain high and the yen stays weak.

The Ministry of Finance will auction about 300 billion yen of 40-year government bonds on Wednesday, reopening an issue first sold in May. The sale could draw demand from insurers and pension funds seeking long-dated debt.

The BOJ is scheduled to buy government bonds in three maturity ranges on Thursday, including those with more than three and up to five years remaining and those with more than 10 and up to 25 years remaining.

Japanese markets will be closed Monday for a national holiday.

China

A thin data slate awaits in China. The sole release of note drops Friday, which will show how China's industrial firms fared in October.

Economists will look at the figures to see if industrial profit growth held up last month after surging in September. Spending tied to artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure has been a key driver of profits over the year, though that hasn't benefited all sectors evenly.

Focus will also be on any potential announcements from Beijing after Xi Jinping's meetings with Trump didn't yield much in the way of progress on key trade and geopolitical issues. Markets will be watching ministry statements closely after Chinese officials warned of potential countermeasures to U.S. moves to tighten chip-export restrictions.

Australia / New Zealand

Australia's October inflation report on Wednesday will help shape expectations for the Reserve Bank of Australia's December rate decision. In September, annual headline inflation rose to 4.3% and trimmed-mean inflation climbed to 3.6%.

Third-quarter capital spending data due Thursday will show how much businesses invested and whether they revised their spending plans. The RBA will publish its bulletin the same day.

In New Zealand, third-quarter retail sales data due Monday will show how household spending is holding up ahead of the central bank's Dec. 9 rate decision.

South Korea

Bank of Korea is expected to raise its benchmark rate by a quarter-percentage-point to 3.25% on Thursday after leaving it unchanged in October.

Some analysts also expect the bank to raise its growth and inflation forecasts for 2026 and 2027 as demand for chips used in artificial intelligence boosts exports and price pressures persist.

The central bank signaled it would raise its growth forecasts after third-quarter gross domestic product grew faster than expected. It expects inflation to stay above its 2% target through 2027.

The International Monetary Fund, the Korea Development Institute and Citi Research raised their growth forecasts for South Korea earlier this month, citing strength in the semiconductor industry.

Singapore

Singapore's consumer-price index likely rose 1.9% in October from a year earlier, down from 2.2% in September, according to the median estimate of six economists polled by The Wall Street Journal. Core inflation, which excludes private road transport and accommodation costs, likely slowed to 1.6% from 2.0%, the poll showed. The data are due Monday.

Lower fourth-quarter electricity tariffs and a high year-earlier comparison likely helped ease inflation, said UOB economist Jester Koh.

Final third-quarter gross domestic product figures are due Tuesday. An advance estimate showed the economy grew 5.4% from a year earlier. DBS economists expect that figure to be revised up to 5.6%, mainly because manufacturing grew faster than initially reported.

DBS expects the government to forecast growth of 2.5% to 4.5% for 2027.

Any references to days are in local times.

data.title: HUTCHMED Initiates RANOVA Phase III Trial of Ranosidenib (HMPL-306) in Patients with IDH-Mutated Glioma in China
data.description:
HONG KONG and SHANGHAI and FLORHAM PARK, N.J., Nov. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- HUTCHMED (China) Limited (“HUTCHMED”) (Nasdaq/AIM:​HCM; HKEX:​13) today announces that it has initiated RANOVA, a registrational Phase III clinical trial of ranosidenib (HMPL-306) in patients with postoperative residual or recurrent Grade 2 gliomas harboring isocitrate dehydrogenase (“IDH”) 1 or 2 mutations in China. Ranosidenib is a novel, highly potent and selective dual inhibitor of IDH1 and IDH2 mutant enzymes. The first patient received the first dose on November 20, 2026.

Gliomas are the most common primary brain tumors, representing around 80% of all primary malignant and central nervous system tumors.1 Worldwide, it is estimated that approximately 260,000 new cases of glioma are diagnosed annually, including nearly 70,000 in China. 2,3 IDH1 or IDH2 mutations are recognized as key oncogenic drivers in the pathogenesis and progression of glioma, found in approximately 70% to 80% of Grade 2 or 3 gliomas, including astrocytoma and oligodendroglioma.4

The trial is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase III study evaluating the efficacy and safety of oral ranosidenib versus placebo in participants with postoperative residual or recurrent Grade 2 astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma carrying IDH1 or IDH2 mutations who have previously received only surgical treatment. Following Blinded Independent Review Committee (“BIRC”)-confirmed disease progression, eligible participants in the placebo group may cross over to receive ranosidenib.

The primary outcome measure is progression-free survival (“PFS”) assessed by BIRC according to Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology (RANO) 2.0 criteria. Secondary outcome measures include investigator-assessed PFS, time to next intervention (TTNI), tumor growth rate (TGR), objective response rate (ORR), overall survival (OS), safety, and quality of life. Additional details may be found at clinicaltrials.gov, using identifier NCT07912398.

This registrational trial plans to enroll approximately 210 patients in China. The leading principal investigators are Professor Jinsong Wu of Huashan Hospital, Fudan University and Professor Xiaohui Ren of Capital Medical University Beijing Tiantan Hospital.

About Ranosidenib

Ranosidenib is a novel dual-inhibitor of IDH1 and IDH2 mutant enzymes. Mutations of IDH1 and IDH2 have been implicated as drivers of certain hematological malignancies, gliomas and solid tumors. Cytoplasmic mutant IDH1 and mitochondrial mutant IDH2 have been known to switch to the other form when targeted by an inhibitor of IDH1 mutant alone or IDH2 mutant alone. Targeting both IDH1 and IDH2 mutations may provide therapeutic benefits in cancer patients by overcoming this acquired resistance.

HUTCHMED currently retains all rights to ranosidenib worldwide.

About HUTCHMED

HUTCHMED (Nasdaq/AIM:HCM; HKEX:13) is an innovative, commercial-stage, biopharmaceutical company. It is committed to the discovery and global development and commercialization of targeted therapies and immunotherapies for the treatment of cancer and immunological diseases. Since inception it has focused on bringing drug candidates from in-house discovery to patients around the world, with its first five medicines marketed in China, the first of which is also approved around the world including in the US, Europe and Japan. For more information, please visit: www.hutch-med.com or follow us on LinkedIn.

data.title: UK government to make case for greater public control of utilities
data.description:
Britain's Labour government will set out details of why it wants more public control of energy and water utilities on Monday when senior minister Louise Haigh addresses the annual conference of lobby group the Confederation of British Industry.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has blamed privatisation of utilities in the 1980s and 1990s, followed by poor regulation, for excess profits, high energy prices and the failure of some water companies to stop releasing sewage into rivers and the sea.

According to Haigh's office, she will tell the CBI that the government wants a new partnership with private capital, "built on clear rules, clear expectations and a fair return on investment".

  • Haigh will say the government does not want "wholesale nationalisation" of utilities, but is concerned that effective monopolies have led to a lack of genuine competition

  • Haigh will also highlight that Britain's utilities sector is an outlier in enabling foreign governments to own significant stakes

  • Burnham set out plans in September to reverse legislation that bars the government from owning more than 3% of water utilities in England and is expected to give more details on utility regulation next month

  • CBI Chief Executive Rain Newton-Smith said she wanted reassurance that greater public control was consistent with "private capital at the table ... not heading for the exit", and would not create undue fears of renationalisation

  • Thames Water – which supplies 16 million customers in and around London – has been regarded as at risk of a costly renationalisation and is restructuring its £20 billion ($26 billion) of debt after mounting fines for pollution

  • In a statement responding to Labour's plans for British utilities, Conservative Party finance spokesperson Andrew Griffith said nationalisation would not lower bills and the government should put less focus on achieving net zero

  • Also at the CBI conference, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage plans to criticise big businesses for backing closer EU ties, which he said would raise regulatory costs for their smaller competitors and let them hire cheaper EU workers instead of Britons

($1 = 0.7645 pounds)

data.title: Automated platform accelerates research on metallic materials
data.description:
TSUKUBA, Japan, Nov 23, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - A new autonomous experimental platform enables fully automated experiments on the structural properties of metallic materials. The system, described in a study published in Science and Technology of Advanced Materials: Methods (STAM-M), offers a basis for closed-loop autonomous optimization of these materials, which will make it easier to develop better structural metals.

Materials science research involves testing a variety of formulations under a range of conditions and measuring many parameters. The number of combinations quickly balloons, and human experimenters can test only a small fraction of those possibilities. That makes autonomous, automated experiments an attractive approach in materials research, but the systems to carry out such experiments need to be developed.

Platforms have been developed to do autonomous, automated experiments with liquids, powders, and thin films, but working with bulk metallic materials has proven challenging. The new system is designed to meet that precise need. "Solid metal specimens are difficult to handle automatically, and the experimental equipment often requires considerable space," explained Yulin Xie of Tohoku University, the study's lead author. "Our platform addresses this challenge by integrating heat treatment, structural analysis, and mechanical testing into a single automated workflow."

The team developed a robotic platform that heats solid metal specimens, examines their structure with X-rays, tests their mechanical properties, and then recovers them. The automated handling, treatment, and recovery of each specimen takes about 13 minutes, not including the time for the heat treatment. All manipulation and measurements are performed automatically. "The platform records how processing affects structure and properties, generating data for AI-based materials development," said Xie.

The researchers tested the platform with automated experiments measuring the properties of an alloy after one- and two-step tempering. The results were consistent with measurements in manual experiments, validating the automated experimental platform. Xie said the team also demonstrated AI-assisted adjustment of the furnace controls, laying the groundwork for closing the automation loop.

The next step is to enable an AI system to set the platform's heat-treatment conditions based on the results of the previous experiment. That would create a closed loop where the results of automated experiments guide the design of the next experiment. "Building on the furnace-control optimization we already demonstrated, we aim to establish an autonomous laboratory that discovers promising heat-treatment routes and accelerates the development of stronger and tougher structural metals," said Xie.

Further information

Yulin Xie

Institute for Materials Research, Tohoku University

yulin.xie.d1@tohoku.ac.jp

Paper: https://doi.org/10.1080/27660400.2026.2735657

About Science and Technology of Advanced Materials: Methods (STAM-M)

STAM Methods is an open access sister journal of Science and Technology of Advanced Materials (STAM), and focuses on emergent methods and tools for improving and/or accelerating materials developments, such as methodology, apparatus, instrumentation, modeling, high-through put data collection, materials/process informatics, databases, and programming. https://www.tandfonline.com/STAM-M

data.title: Clariant, CD&R  in talks to acquire chemicals firm Ashland - Bloomberg
data.description:
Clariant AG and private equity firm CD&R are in discussions to buy chemicals maker Ashland .

The Swiss specialty chemicals company and the PE firm are negotiating an all-cash deal that values Ashland close to its share price on Friday, according to a Bloomberg report on Sunday, which cited people familiar with the matter. A transaction could come together as soon as the coming days.

No final decision has been made, and talks could fall apart, or another suitor could still emerge, the people told Bloomberg.

Ashland and Clariant declined to comment. A spokesperson for CD&R didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

A potential deal comes as activist investors have been pushing for months for Ashland to explore a sale. In August, Ashland confirmed an agreement with activist investor Ancora Holdings to expand the chemical maker's board.

Last month Dealreporter said that CD&R was partnering with Clariant ( for a bid for Ashland ).

data.title: Dow Jones, Nasdaq futures rebound up to 600 points - This is the most important trigger of the week
data.description:
Futures on Wall Street are looking to stage a rebound as trading resumed on Sunday evening US time following their worst week in years. This week happens to be a truncated one for the US markets as well.

Futures on the Dow Jones are trading with gains between 450 - 500 points. The S&P 500 futures are up over 100 points, while the Nasdaq futures are up over 600 points at the start of trading in the futures market.

Wall Street is aiming for a rebound after the Dow Jones and the Nasdaq reported their worst weekly performance since March 2020, which was the onset of the Covid-19 pandemic. The Dow fell 8% last week, while the Nasdaq corrected 10%. At its intraday low on Friday, the Nasdaq 100 index has slipped into "bear market territory", meaning a fall of 20% or more from the peak.

S&P 500's 3.5% fall last week was also its worst weekly performance since April 2025, which marked US President Donald Trump's Liberation Day tariff announcements. The S&P 500 closed below its 200-Day Moving Average on Friday, and Edward Yardeni, of Yardeni Research, cut his target on the index to 7,500 for the year-end from 7,900 earlier. However, he still believes that the index will end 2027 between 8,500 - 9,000 levels.

A combination of multiple factors, profit booking due to the mega Anthropic IPO, issues surrounding Nvidia, breaking of key technical levels, worries of the Federal Reserve hiking interest rates aggressively, are all contributing to the sell-off in the US markets.

The sell-off has resulted in investors flocking to haven assets, with the US 10-year bond yield slumping back to 4.95% from 5.12% on Thursday. The US Dollar index also traded near the mark of 104, sparking a broader sell-off in metals.

The Biggest Trigger For Wall Street This Week

As this is a truncated week, most of the macroeconomic data will be reported during the first three days of the week itself.

Before the macro data is reported, two key hardware companies, Hewlett Packard Enterprises, and Dell, will be reporting their quarterly results after market closing hours on Monday and Tuesday respectively. HPE shares are down 25% this month so far, while Dell shares have slumped 34%.

The biggest trigger for the week though, will be the Personal Consumption Expenditure (PCE) inflation data, which will be reported on Wednesday. This is the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge and will be the final inflation print before the Fed rate decision on December 9.

As of today, the probability of the Fed raising rates by 25 basis points on December 9, still stands at 89%.

Second estimates of the Q3 GDP data, consumer spending print, jobless claims, wholesale and retail inventories data will also be reported during the course of the week.

data.title: Prairie Lithium Brings Saskatchewan Brine to Surface Ahead of Processing Tests
data.description:
Prairie Lithium has recovered brine for the next stage of work on its proposed lithium operation after completing the first production-well test at its namesake project’s Pad #1 in Saskatchewan.

The milestone follows a well re-entry program that opened production zones in the Duperow Formation, moving the project beyond site preparation and into testing material from the reservoir.

Civil works have meanwhile expanded the operating area for the first development stage, where a commercial-scale extraction unit has already been delivered but has yet to be integrated.

For Prairie, the result fulfils the initial production-testing milestone it had scheduled for the final quarter of 2026, although commercial lithium production remains a separate objective.

With lithium market conditions influencing the pace of spending, Prairie is concentrating on work needed to establish its processing route before committing to the next phase of construction.

Additional Working Space

At Pad #1, grading and contouring have provided additional working space around infrastructure built during earlier phases of the project.

The production and disposal wells, electricity infrastructure, and facility building were already in place when the latest expansion was completed.

A four-column commercial-scale direct lithium extraction unit has also arrived, leaving installation and integration among the important tasks still ahead.

Further preparations cover pre-treatment and lithium chloride concentration systems, while procurement planning continues for processing equipment and the balance of plant.

Prairie has a binding offtake agreement with Hydro Lithium covering all planned Phase 1 production, although the agreement does not change the remaining construction and commissioning requirements.

Perforation and Swabbing

A local service rig re-entered the production well and completed perforation and swabbing work that brought brine to the surface ahead of the Canadian winter.

The recovered brine will now go into further metallurgical testing, allowing the developer to examine the material that would ultimately pass through its planned processing facilities.

It is a practical next step for a project whose staged development depends on bringing together well operations, extraction equipment, and downstream processing rather than any one of those elements in isolation.

“Completing the site expansion, civil works and re-entry program ahead of the Canadian winter is another positive step in preparing Pad #1 for the next stages of development,” executive chair Paul Lloyd said.

“The recovered brine will now be used for continued metallurgical testing as we advance our Phase 1 plans.”

‘Measured and Disciplined Approach’

Approved interest-free financing of approximately A$6.6 million (C$6.3m) from the Canadian government is intended to support procurement and installation of the first-stage equipment and associated plant systems.

Even with that funding in place, management is keeping the sequence and pace of investment under review rather than setting out a fixed timetable for completing the operation.

“Considering the current commodity price environment and broader market conditions, the company is taking a measured and disciplined approach to capital allocation,” Mr Lloyd added.

“We remain focused on progressing critical-path construction activities at site while carefully managing expenditure to preserve the project’s long term value and flexibility.”

For now, the immediate work is to evaluate the recovered brine and prepare the extraction and concentration equipment for integration, with subsequent activity dependent on funding, project requirements, and market conditions.
